text:
sam-cs: FYI customer (acme) reporting intermittent 503/504s on hosted embeddings this morning. started ~08:10UTC, happening across regions but higher in us-west1. they say it spikes with large batch calls (>16 inputs).

maria-support: Thanks — can you drop their repro steps here? we need copy for eng and SRE.

sam-cs: Repro from customer: `POST /v1/embeddings` with model `embed-large-v2`, payload ~20–30 short strings, concurrency 8 clients. They see ~10% 503 and then client SDK retries cause duplicate billing. sample curl:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_TOKEN" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","inputs":["q1","q2",..."q25"]}'
```

anya-eng-runtime: tagging eng-runtime. Initial glance: 503 at gateway level or upstream? can you paste a raw response body from customer (if they have it) and approximate timestamps?

acme-support-contact: here's a sample response body and headers we captured: `{"error":"upstream timeout","code":503}`. request id: rwid=acme-2026-03-17-08:15:22. sent from us-west1.

tyler-sre: I pulled traces for rwid=acme-2026-03-17-08:15:22 — gateway returned 502 after 9s. upstream inference node reported kvcache lock wait >8s then connection closed. looks like lock contention on kvcache when many parallel batch requests hit the same model shard.

anya-eng-runtime: that matches a recent change to cache sharding heuristics (PR #4821) that tightened shard affinity for latency. possible regression where hot prefixes collide. assign to me to reproduce locally.

maria-support: Customer impact: multiple customers on dedicated tenancy saw increased 5xx rate during acme's spike. acme asks for ETA and temporary mitigation.

sam-cs: Can we give acme a short-term mitigation? they asked for a rollback option or temporary routing to a fallback model.

tyler-sre: Temp mitigations we can do now: 1) reduce acme's max_concurrency to 2 at the gateway, 2) route their traffic to `embed-large-v2-quant` (different shard mapping), or 3) apply backpressure by lowering batch_size to 8. I can patch a rate-limit for tenant=acme until a fix.

anya-eng-runtime: I'll try to repro with a load script: concurrent clients=8, batch_size=25, model=embed-large-v2, run against a staging cluster with the same sharding. if I can reproduce I'll bisect PRs.

maria-support: Please keep communications short — customer wants a timeline. Sam, propose: apply concurrency cap now + route to fallback model, update them in 30m, and follow up when eng confirms root cause.

sam-cs: pinging acme with temporary mitigation plan. will ask for permission to throttle to 2 concurrent requests and route new calls to `embed-large-v2-quant` for 1 hour.

acme-support-contact: ok to throttle. please do the fallback routing. we'll monitor. thanks.

deploy-bot: roll started by tyler-sre: applying tenant rate-limit patch for tenant=acme (config-id rl-9412)

tyler-sre: patch applied at 08:37UTC. metrics show acme 5xx drop from 9% -> 1.8% in 5m. backpressure prevented repeat failures but throughput dropped ~25%.

anya-eng-runtime: repro successful in staging: replicated kvcache lock contention with our load script. root cause narrowed to affinity change in PR #4821 + some high-cardinality prefix traffic pattern. will open a revert + targeted fix.

maria-support: ETA for fix? customer is asking for an SLA note and rollback confirmation.

anya-eng-runtime: I'm preparing a revert PR now, target is to merge and deploy to staging within 2h, prod in 4h pending QA. I'll post PR link when ready.

sam-cs: Updated acme: we've throttled concurrent calls and routed to fallback model, seeing reduced errors. eng is working on a fix and we expect a patch within ~4 hours. will update if anything changes. :thumbsup:

acme-support-contact: thanks for the quick response. please keep us posted.

tyler-sre: follow-up: monitoring for other tenants — none show elevated error rates after the mitigation. continuing to watch.

anya-eng-runtime: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/4821-revert-kv-affinity. I put a test manifest to exercise hot-prefixes. requesting expedited review.

maria-support: Great — once deployed to prod we'll coordinate with CS to un-throttle and revert fallback routing. Sam, prepare a short customer-facing postmortem template.

sam-cs: Will draft and share in #support-postmortems.

tyler-sre: last note — if anyone needs to reproduce quickly here's my load command: `python tools/load_test.py --concurrency 8 --batch-size 25 --model embed-large-v2 --tenant acme --duration 2m`

anya-eng-runtime: thanks, I'll use that and capture flamegraphs.

sam-cs: closing the customer loop for now; will re-open thread when we have a deploy+postmortem.
